observations: Photo 0: one flat panel TV leaning against a wall on a tiled floor, seen from the front at an angle.
The screen is switched off; it only reflects the room. No picture, so pixels and lines cannot be judged.
Thin silver or grey metal bezel, no visible crack or chip on the glass in this view.
No brand logo, model plate, back panel or rear label is readable in photo 0.
No stand or feet are attached; no remote is shown.
Size cannot be measured: there is no reference object or tape, though the panel looks large.

identity.kind: flat screen TV, large size, brand not readable
read_from: photo 0 front view, no logo or label legible

claims.evidence: No Samsung logo or label can be read in photo 0; the bezel shows no legible text.
No size label, model number or tape measure in photo 0.
Screen is off in photo 0; no home screen or apps shown.

claims.claim: No dead pixel, no line on the screen
claims.evidence: Screen is off in photo 0; needs a clip of the TV on a plain white and a plain black picture.
Repair history cannot be shown in a photo; only opening the back would hint at it.

risks.risk: Brand and model are not as claimed; a lesser brand or older model sets a much lower price.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the label on the back of the TV showing brand, model number and serial.
risks.if_unproven: Cannot set even a worst case without it; the model plate is what sets the price.

risks.risk: TV does not power on, or the panel has dead pixels, lines or backlight bleed.
risks.proof: A clip of the TV switching on and showing a full white, full black and full colour screen, with the model shown in the settings menu.

risks.risk: Screen size is smaller than 55 inch.
risks.proof: Back label photo with the model number, or a tape measure across the diagonal of the screen.
risks.if_unproven: As the smallest size consistent with the photo.

risks.proof: A photo of the stand or feet next to the TV.
A photo of the remote next to the TV, and the clip showing it changing channels.

risks.risk: Board or panel has been repaired or replaced.
risks.proof: A photo of the back panel screws and label, showing no tampering.

proof_requests: Photo of the label on the back of the TV showing brand, model number and serial.
Clip of the TV powering on, showing full white, full black and colour screens, and the model page in settings.
Photo of the front bezel logo and the stand or feet.
Photo of the remote, and the clip showing it working.
Tape measure across the screen diagonal if the back label is unreadable.
response.reason: Photo 0 shows a switched-off flat screen TV with no readable logo or label, so the brand, model and size that set a TV's price are all unproven. The back label photo and a power-on clip are needed before even a worst case price can be set.
